description: We are a team passionate about space, AI/ML, data science, and technology. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to explore NASA’s open data, develop creative solutions, and solve real-world challenges through teamwork, innovation, and collaboration
summary: AstroHealth is a self-health-monitoring app for astronauts on long missions, with ASTRA, a voice and chat medical assistant. On a Mars mission, help from Earth can be about 20 minutes away each way, so astronauts must be able to assess their own health. The app guides a daily self-exam of 10 indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, temperature, oxygen, sleep, mood, exercise, hydration and cabin CO2), explaining how to measure each one and why spaceflight affects it. Results appear on a colour-coded dashboard (green, amber, red) and a clickable body map. The app learns each astronaut's personal baseline, flags unusual readings early, forecasts when a reading may leave its healthy range, and links changes to NASA's five spaceflight hazards. It gives plain-language advice, emergency steps, a Mars communication-delay mode that guides the astronaut on board and queues messages for Earth, and a one-click flight surgeon report. It works offline and includes gamification (streaks, XP and a readiness score). ASTRA answers medical questions by text and voice.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

AstroHealth helps astronauts check their own health during long missions to the Moon or Mars, when doctors on Earth may be minutes away. It guides the astronaut through a daily self-exam, shows the results at a glance, explains what they mean, and tells them what to do next.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Guided self-exam: 10 indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, temperature, oxygen, sleep, mood, exercise, hydration, cabin CO2). Each step explains how to measure and why spaceflight affects it, so no medical background is needed.

2. Dashboard and body map: every reading is coloured green, amber or red. Clicking the brain, lungs, heart, metabolism or bones shows its status and how space affects it.

3. Personal baseline: the app learns each astronaut's own normal from their recent readings and warns when a reading drifts, even before it is out of range. It also forecasts when a reading may leave its healthy range.

4. Hazard insights: readings and mission context feed a risk score for each of NASA's five spaceflight hazards (radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, closed environment).

5. Mission-aware advice: the astronaut picks Space Station, Lunar Base, Mars Transit or Mars Surface. With a long delay, the app gives on-board emergency steps and queues messages for Earth.

6. Flight surgeon report: one click creates a printable summary of readings, alerts and trends.

7. ASTRA assistant: a medical-only chatbot that answers by text and by voice.

8. Offline mode and gamification: data is saved on the device so the app works without internet, and streaks, XP, quests and a Mission Readiness Score keep astronauts engaged.

BENEFITS

Faster self-assessment, earlier warnings, clear guidance when help is far away, and better information for flight surgeons.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

A tool that could support astronaut autonomy on future missions, extended with real wearables and clinically validated rules.

TOOLS

React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Apache ECharts, Recharts, Zustand, Dexie (IndexedDB), vite-plugin-pwa, Lucide, Node.js and Express. ASTRA uses a large language model and Whisper speech-to-text through an OpenAI-compatible API (Groq). Deployed on Vercel and Render.

LIMITATIONS

This is a prototype. Readings are simulated or demo data, healthy ranges and advice are prototype rules that are not clinically validated, and it is not a medical device.

SI (AI) USE

AI tools helped write parts of the code, including the interface and the analysis engine, and ASTRA uses AI models at runtime. The challenge selection, feature list and direction came from our team. (See the README in our GitHub repository.)
